sentence_stem: Although the house had been painted only last year,
correct_completion: it was already showing signs of damage.
full_sentence: Although the house had been painted only last year, it was already showing signs of damage.
acceptable_variants: water was already leaking through the roof.
the walls had already started to crack.

options.text: so the owners decided to sell it.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a result, not a contrast. 'Although' needs a clause that contrasts with the first part of the sentence.

options.text: the paint had been chosen by a designer.
options.why_wrong: This adds background information about the painting but does not create the contrast that 'although' requires.

options.text: it was already showing signs of damage.
the windows were being cleaned every day.
options.why_wrong: This describes a routine task, which does not contrast with the idea of the house having been recently painted.

explanation: After 'although', we need a clause that shows contrast with the first part of the sentence. Here the recent painting is contrasted with the damage that has already appeared. Learners often add a result connector such as 'so' here, because their first language may use cause and result phrasing more readily than concession.
translation: Хоча будинок було пофарбовано лише минулого року, на ньому вже з'являлися ознаки пошкоджень.
